operation_details.item: The user prefers prose-only system design documents with no diagrams, sequence flows, or component boundaries.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How’s the architecture work going today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well. I’m drafting the design for the service split we discussed.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice. Are you planning to include the usual diagrams and sequence flows?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Actually, I prefer keeping system design documents prose-only. I find that a clear narrative is easier to maintain than diagrams or rigid component-boundary sections.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense, especially if the architecture is still changing. You could describe the request path and responsibilities directly in the text.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I’ll explain the tradeoffs, data flow, and operational concerns in plain sections without adding visual artifacts.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Sounds focused. Are you reviewing it with the team this afternoon?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, I’m aiming to circulate a draft before lunch so they can comment on the implementation details.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that In system design documents, I want prose-only descriptions with no diagrams, sequence flows, or component boundaries.
